newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's PUMA says govt plans tax change.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's PUMA says govt plans tax change.

text.p: Macquarie Bank Ltd securitisation vehicle PUMA Managment Ltd said on Friday the Australian government plans to amend interest withholding tax legislation.
The 10 percent interest withholding tax had been an obstacle to PUMA raising funds offshore to lend to Australian home buyers because the tax had to be passed on to local borrowers.

PUMA said the legislation specifically referred to the use of funds for home loans, and now means that institutions like PUMA can now access the cheapest source of capital available, whether that means raising funds domestically or offshore.

"We are now able to raise funds offshore, which will allow Aussie Home Loans and others to continue to pass on sustainable benefits to Australian home owners and small business borrowers," said PUMA Management Director, Tony Gill.
"The ability to raise funds offshore will allow PUMA to expand and diversify its funding base, aiming for an even cheaper cost of funds," Gill said.
PUMA announced last week a A$3.0 billion funding programme for 1997, with a portion of that funding to be raised offshore, subject to market conditions.
Gill added that government's decision to change the withholding tax legislation meant the maintenance of a competitive environment for Australian borrowers.
